summary: Players simultaneously reveal a hand card each round and slot it into one of four ascending rows, taking the whole row (and its penalty bull's-heads) if their card is the sixth added; the tension comes from guessing how close your number is to the current row-ends and fearing being forced into a bad row. It's fast, light, and mean in a friendly way, with almost no direct control over your fate beyond calculated bluffing on card values.
praised: Extremely quick to teach and play
Tense push-your-luck decisions despite simple rules
Scales well from small to large groups
Great as a filler or gateway game
criticised: Heavy luck/randomness in hand draw and turn order reveal
Can feel mean when you're forced to eat a big row
Limited long-term depth or replayable strategy
Some feel it overstays its welcome at higher player counts

interaction.kind: Simultaneous card placement forcing indirect blocking and row denial

scoring.why: The game ends when a player crosses a bull's-head penalty threshold, and the player with the fewest accumulated penalty points wins
